text.p: Wesfarmers Ltd said on Tuesday it expected continued revenue and earnings growth in the year to June 30, 1998 following a jump in 1996/97 revenue and earnings.
Wesfarmers said it also planned to spend A$500 million on capital expenditure of its businesses in 1997/98, up from A$185 million in 1996/97.

"The directors expect continued growth in revenue and earnings in the 1997/98 financial year," Wesfarmers said in a statement accompanying its 1996/97 results. The company reported a net profit of A$139.55 million, up from A$92.79 million a year earlier. Sales rose to A$2.60 billion from A$2.43 billion.

"The directors continue to support the expansion of existing business operations with a substantial capital investment programme," the company said. "Expenditure of about A$500 million is budgeted for 1997/98," it said.
Wesfarmers said strong growth in 1997/98 would be generated from the expanding hardware warehouse chain, including new stores to be opened in New South Wales and Queensland.
The expected upturn in the housing market should also lift earnings, the company said.
Wesfarmers said the fertiliser/chemical unit, which comes under the Wesfarmers CSBP unit, increased EBIT by 51 percent to A$83.6 million in 1996/97.

The hardware and forest products unit increased EBIT by 21 percent to A$46.8 million in the year. EBIT for the rural and insurance unit was A$22.1 million in 1996/97, compared with A$1.7 million a year earlier.
At 1.45 p.m. (0345 GMT), Wesfarmers shares were up 46 cents or 3.80 to A$12.55 on low volume.
